input.title: Discounts on patient invoices before payment
input.text: Allow authorised users to apply discounts to patient invoices before collecting payment. The final payable amount must be recalculated and reflected in payment records, patient billing history and revenue reports.

current.text: There is no patient invoice in the code. A patient's fee for one visit is stored as two numbers on that visit's row in the medical_report table: fee_charged and fee_paid.
Consultation fees and therapy fees are kept separately inside the visit's recommendations JSON, not in their own columns.

The doctor types fee charged, fee paid, consultation fees and therapy fees as four separate whole numbers (digits only, at most 5 characters). Nothing calculates one from another, and nothing checks that fee paid is not more than fee charged.

The amount still owed is always worked out on read as fee charged minus fee paid: in patient billing history (remainingFees), the patient portal (clientRemainingFees), the patient's login summary, the dashboard totals and the Fee-Info section of generated reports.
Monthly revenue on the doctor dashboard is the sum of fee_charged for the month, for the logged-in doctor only.
The appointment notification only carries the doctor's UPI id and QR code, with no amount.

No patient payment table exists: the payment-related tables (transactions, pg_order_details, ashoka_payment_orders, corporate_payments) have no patient, visit or medical id in their model fillable lists (a free JSON column such as transactions.invoice_data was not inspected), and belong to subscriptions, device orders and corporate billing. The only patient payment record is fee_paid on the visit.

Discounts exist today only for subscription plans (the doctor paying for Nadi Tarangini): a coupon gives a percentage discount on the plan price. This is a different flow and a different table, not patient fees.

Saving fees has no role check. The visit lookup has its doctor filter commented out; the only ownership check is that the patient belongs to the caller or to a doctor the caller is allowed to act for (allowed_functions).

Role id 4 is "College"; id 5 was renamed "Receptionist". Roles named Admin (7), Assistant and Billing also exist. For College users the visit ends at the diet step and fee charged and fee paid end up 0: some diet-save paths send zeros explicitly, others send no amounts and the backend stores 0 for missing values.

Per-user feature permissions already exist: the NT admin panel stores each user's allowed features in user_personal_info.allowed_functions, from a feature list kept in master_contents (type nt_hardcoded_features).
The medical visit report given to the patient shows FEE CHARGED and FEE PAID.
patient/remainingFees has no caller in the web app or the mobile app.

proposed.text: Store the discount as a new whole-number amount per visit on medical_report. fee_charged keeps its meaning (price before discount). Payable = fee_charged - discount; still owed = payable - fee_paid.
The patient's doctor may always give a discount; any other user only when the NT admin grants a new "Give discount" feature in their allowed features. Patients and College users cannot.
Revenue on the dashboard is shown after discounts, with the total discount alongside.
The discount can be changed until the visit is closed; who gave it, when and why are stored.
The medical visit report and partner report data show the discount and payable amount as new fields; existing fields keep their names and meaning.

objective.text: Let clinics give patients a discount and keep what is owed, collected and earned consistent everywhere it is shown.

summary.headline: Adding a discount changes how a visit's fee is stored and how the amount owed and earned is worked out, and that number is read by billing history, the patient portal, the dashboard and every generated report.

consequences.text: Every place that works out the amount owed as fee charged minus fee paid must be changed together. If one is missed, the patient, the doctor and the reports show different amounts for the same visit.
Fee saving has no role check, so "authorised users" needs a permission that does not exist yet.

Three web methods and the app send the fee fields by name; each must send the discount. Four more web diet-save calls, for users with role id 4, send no fees or zeros, and today that resets fee charged and fee paid to 0.
Whether revenue goes down after a discount depends on a product decision: today it is the sum of fee charged.

patients.description: Patient records and the backend fee save (patient/saveFees) and patient billing history (patient/remainingFees).
patients.why_affected: It owns the code that stores the visit fee and works out the amount still owed.

functional_impact.text: saveFees must accept, check and store the discount and the payable amount next to fee_charged and fee_paid.
remainingFees adds up fee charged minus fee paid over all of a patient's visits; it must take the discount into account.
The previous-visit lists return fee_charged and fee_paid per visit, so the visit history the doctor sees would not show the discount unless they change too.

nadi-flow.description: The visit flow, including the fee step on the web and in the app.
nadi-flow.why_affected: The fee form and the web controllers that forward fees to the backend are here.

functional_impact.text: The web fee form needs a discount field and must show the payable amount before saving.
saveFeesData and saveFeesDataWithNA pass each fee field by name to patient/saveFees; a new field is not passed unless added.
The app fee tab builds the request body field by field; it needs a discount field too.
For users with role id 4, four diet-save calls also call patient/saveFees with no fee fields or with zeros, which resets fee charged and fee paid to 0. These paths must not reset a discount.

functional_impact.text: Monthly revenue is the sum of fee_charged; it needs a decision on gross or net and a matching change.
Total remaining is total charged minus total paid; with a discount it would show discounted amounts as still owed.
The web dashboard shows fee paid and fee remaining from these totals; the app dashboard reads the same fields.

workflow.before: Types fee charged, fee paid, consultation and therapy fees as separate numbers.
workflow.after: Also enters a discount; the form shows the payable amount (fee charged minus discount).
workflow.on_failure: A wrong payable amount on screen means the wrong amount is collected from the patient.

workflow.before: Three web methods and the app forward the fee fields by name; four role-4 diet-save calls send no fees or zeros.
workflow.after: Every path forwards the discount, or leaves an existing discount untouched.
workflow.on_failure: A path that does not forward the discount saves the visit at full price, or resets it.

workflow.before: Checks each fee is a whole number and stores fee_charged and fee_paid (0 when missing).
workflow.after: Checks the user may give a discount and that the discount is within limits, then stores the discount and the payable amount.
workflow.on_failure: The save is rolled back and the visit cannot be finished ("Fees not added"); or an unchecked discount is stored and the amount owed is misstated.

workflow.before: Collects payment outside the system (the notification offers UPI or QR) and types the amount as fee paid.
workflow.after: Collects the payable amount and records it as fee paid.
workflow.on_failure: Fee paid is compared with the wrong amount, so the visit shows as under- or over-paid.

workflow.before: Amount still owed = sum of fee charged minus sum of fee paid.
workflow.after: Amount still owed = sum of payable minus sum of fee paid.
workflow.on_failure: The patient or doctor sees the discount as still owed.

workflow.before: Revenue = sum of fee charged for the month; remaining = charged minus paid.
workflow.after: Revenue is shown net of discounts, with total discount alongside (A5); remaining = payable minus paid.
workflow.on_failure: Revenue is overstated, or does not match billing history.

workflow.before: Each report's Fee-Info shows fee charged, paid and remaining (charged minus paid).
workflow.after: The medical visit report and partner Fee-Info show the discount and payable amount as new fields (A8).
workflow.on_failure: Reports give the patient a different amount from the one the doctor collected.

data_fields.change: New whole-number amount per visit (A4); a percentage, if entered, is converted to an amount on the server (A9).
Meaning kept: price before discount (A4), so existing readers stay correct.
Not linked to fee_charged today; the discount applies to the visit total, not to these components (A4).

data_fields.calculation: total_revenue = SUM(fee_charged - discount) for the month

data_consistency.text: The amount owed is computed separately in eight places (remainingFees, clientRemainingFees, handlePatientLogin, getUserSummary and the fetchFeeInfo of four report services).
data_consistency.consequence: If any of them is not changed, different screens and reports show different amounts owed for the same visit.

data_consistency.text: saveFees stores 0 for fee_charged and fee_paid when they are not sent (consultation and therapy fees are left unchanged when missing), and four role-4 web diet-save calls send no fees or zeros.
data_consistency.consequence: If the discount is saved the same way, a later save from one of those paths could reset the discount.

data_consistency.text: Fee values are whole numbers only (integer validation, digits-only input).
data_consistency.consequence: A percentage discount needs a rounding rule, or the payable amount and the collected amount can differ by a rupee.

data_consistency.text: Visits saved before the change have no discount value.
data_consistency.consequence: Readers must treat a missing discount as 0, or old visits show wrong amounts.

risks.reason: If steps 1-3 fail, the visit cannot be finished ("Fees not added"), or a wrong payable amount is shown, dropped or reset. Payment itself is collected outside the system, so this is rated FAIL-02 (core workflow) rather than FAIL-01 (money movement); see Q13.
risks.consequence: the visit flow breaks, or the wrong amount is collected and recorded as owed or paid

risks.reason: "Authorised users" needs a permission check, but fee saving has no role check, and the visit lookup's doctor filter is commented out. The only check is that the patient belongs to the caller or to a doctor the caller is allowed to act for.
risks.consequence: any user allowed to see that doctor's patients, whatever their role, could give a discount

assumptions.text: A "patient invoice" means the fee record of one visit in medical_report, the only patient fee record found, and discounts apply to patient visit fees, not subscription plans.
Discounts are limited to the fee charged and only some users may give them.

Decision (Claude, at the user's request, from the code): the patient's doctor may always give a discount; other users only with a new "Give discount" feature granted in the NT admin feature list (allowed_functions); patients (role 2) and College users (role 4) cannot. Roles such as Billing, Admin or Receptionist get it only when granted.
Decision: a single whole-number discount amount on the visit total (not on consultation or therapy fees), 0 <= discount <= fee_charged; fee_charged keeps its meaning (price before discount).
Decision: dashboard revenue is net of discounts (sum of fee_charged minus discount), with the total discount shown beside it.
Decision: a discount can be changed until the visit is closed; who gave it, when and the reason are stored with the visit, and fee_paid above the payable amount is refused.
Decision: saveFees also checks that the visit's doctor is the caller or a doctor the caller may act for (the same allowed ids already used for the patient check).
Decision: the medical visit report and the partner Fee-Info add discount and payable amount as new fields; existing fields keep their names and meaning, so partners are not broken.
Decision: if a percentage is entered, the server converts it to a whole amount rounded to the nearest unit and stores the amount.

Answered from code: the patient "invoice" is the visit's fee record; "payment records" means fee_paid; College users' zero-fee diet saves are by design and keep the discount at 0; patient/remainingFees has no client caller but is updated too for consistency.

actions.text: Confirm the recommended decisions A3-A9 (Q1, Q2, Q4, Q6, Q10).
Change the eight places that compute the amount owed together, and add the discount to the three web save methods and the app.
Add a "Give discount" feature to the NT admin feature list and check it in saveFees, plus the visit-doctor check (A7).
Add medical_report to the money tables in config/impact-signals.yaml (Q9).
Run the web scenarios on staging and test the app fee tab and dashboard by hand (not covered by web QA).
